output.name: Varuk
output.gloss: The Kite Aun Did Not Fly

anatomy.part: top corner of the kite body
lower corner of the kite, where the tail is tied
end of the streamer, the cut thread
stone weight hanging at the tail's end

output.myth: Aun wanted a second kite to fetch the first one back. Ennu the Kite-Wright cut cloth from the best sail and bone from the oldest goat, and Aun worked until his fingers split. He hung a stone on the tail so it would ride low, and tied the string to his own wrist. Then Tavo came up off the water laughing and snatched the kite before it had lifted. Aun was too proud to chase it. Hesk keeps count of every string, and she has counted this one. The kite never flew. It hangs in the Leeward with its stone at the bottom, and its thread runs out to a spark no one has reached. On still nights the old women say you can hear it knocking against the lamps, and that it is only Aun, pretending he is about to go out.
